content.title: About
content.content: Overripe raw plantains (Musa paradisiaca) are the unripe fruits of banana‑like plants harvested when the skin has begun to darken and the flesh is soft but not fully sweet. They have a mildly sweet aroma, creamy texture, and a faint tang.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Plantains are a staple in African, Caribbean, and Latin American cuisines.
Raw overripe plantains are rich in resistant starch, which acts as a prebiotic.
Unlike bananas, plantains are usually cooked, but some cultures enjoy them raw in salads.
The fruits grow in bunches containing 10–20 plantains each.
Plantains thrive in tropical and subtropical climates with warm, humid conditions.

items.title: High in complex carbohydrates
items.content: They provide slowly digestible starch that helps maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and acts as an antioxidant.

items.title: Rich in potassium
items.content: Potassium aids blood‑pressure regulation and heart function.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber promotes intestinal motility and a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Solanine content
items.content: Unripe plantains may contain small amounts of solanine, which can be toxic in large doses.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to banana‑family plants.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Excessive raw plantain consumption can cause bloating and gas due to high resistant starch.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw overripe plantains can be thinly sliced and added to salads, pickled, blended into smoothies, or used as a base for vegan “chips.” They are also commonly boiled or stewed, but raw they work well as quick snacks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store plantains in the refrigerator’s crisper drawer, wrapped in parchment paper to slow further ripening. Discard any that develop strong off‑odors or mold.
